**Result: 16 active USCG notices fall within 1 nm of your route (14.35 nm). The check was partial, so don't treat this as a complete clearance.**

The check ran at 2026-10-08 21:03 UTC with a 1 nm corridor on each side. Nothing was upcoming or expired. The one safety-zone dataset I couldn't check is described at the end.

**Notices that intersect the route itself**
- **Survey operations (Monmouth Univ./Equinor), through Nov 1.** The R/V OCEAN HAWK is recovering unmarked seafloor moorings in New York Harbor and along the export cable corridor. The notice says the moorings have no surface buoys and the vessel monitors VHF 16/13. It intersects near the southern leg, about 15% along the route.
- **Sailing regatta, Upper Bay south of Governors Island, through Oct 18.** It runs Wed/Thu 6–9 pm, Sat 12–5 pm, and Sun Oct 18 12–5 pm. It is about 35% along the route.
- **Three weekly sailing regattas, Upper Bay between Ellis and Governors Islands, 6:30–8:00 pm.** One runs Tuesdays through Oct 13, one Wednesdays through Oct 14, and one Thursdays through Oct 15. They are about 49% along the route and use VHF 68.
- **Manhattan circumnavigation swim events, through Oct 13.** Swimmers are escorted by safety vessels and kayaks. Oct 8–13 starts are mostly morning to mid-afternoon from Pier A (VHF 6). It is about 56% along the route.

**Notices near the route but not on it**
- **Sunken barge hazard, Anchorage 21-A.** It is 0.07 nm from the route and in effect through Mar 27, 2027. The barge is in about 13 ft of water and marked by 4 buoys with strobes.
- **Marine construction.** Several sites sit within 1 nm of your track:
  - Governors Island fender wharf rehab, 0.68 nm away, weekdays through Nov 30.
  - Liberty State Park barges, 0.54 nm away, through Oct 31.
  - Trevcon/Battery Park City work at Reaches 06 and 02 and the North Cove dredging, 0.003–0.03 nm away. These have barges moved by tug at any hour, run through 2027–2029, and monitor VHF 13/16/65–75.
  - Hudson Tunnel Project cofferdam and barges off Pier 66, 0.52 nm away, through Jan 2027.
  - Manhattan Cruise Terminal dredging, 0.58 nm away, through Oct 10, 24 hours a day, on VHF 78/13/16.
  - Pier 94 pile repairs, 0.52 nm away, through June 2027.
- **Safety zone, 33 CFR 165.T01-0336, Hudson River off Pier 66.** It is 0.52 nm from the route and enforced through Jan 20, 2029. Entry needs COTP New York permission on VHF 16 or (718) 354-4353. This zone is not on your track, but you would need that permission if you deviated into it.

**Limits of this check**
- **Safety-zone coverage is incomplete.** NAVCEN's `safeZoneLine_1` dataset returned a 404 and wasn't checked. Line-type safety zones could therefore be missing.
- **Out of scope:** Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, aids-to-navigation discrepancies, NOAA/NGA warnings, AIS, weather and tides.
- **Not navigational advice.** Before you go, confirm with the current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, VHF broadcasts and Captain of the Port New York.

finalAnswer:
Yes. The U.S. Coast Guard's navigation safety feed (NAVCEN) lists 14 notices within 1 nautical mile of a straight line between your two points. Most are dredging and construction work in the Houston Ship Channel and Galveston Bay. None is a formal closure, but several ask vessels to coordinate, slow down or avoid meeting near the work. The check ran on 2026-10-08.

**Caveat:** the Coast Guard's safety-zone layer, which holds formal closures and security zones, was not published and couldn't be checked. So I can't rule out a safety zone on this route. Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices and non-Coast Guard sources (NOAA, NGA, AIS, weather) were also not covered.

**Dredging and marine construction (in effect)**
- **Galveston Bay pipeline installation (until about 2027-03-01):**
  - It sits east of Houston Ship Channel Light 42, about a third of the way along your route.
  - Crews and vessels work 24 hours a day.
  - By about Nov 1, equipment will be within 1,800 ft of both sides of the channel.
  - Transit at your slowest safe speed.
- **Houston Ship Channel dredging between Lights 78 and 92 (Dredge R.B. Weeks, ends 2026-10-10):**
  - It runs 24/7.
  - Avoid meeting or overtaking near the dredges.
  - Contact them on VHF 13 or 16.
- **Barbours Cut dredging (Dredge DB Catalina, until further notice):**
  - It is within 0.03 nm of your route.
  - The dredge asks for 30 minutes' notice if you are going to or from Barbours Terminal Channel.
  - Contact them on VHF 13 or 81.
- **Morgans Point and Barbours Terminal dredging and bulkhead work (until 2027-07-01):**
  - It runs 24/7.
  - Watch for dive flags and day shapes.
  - Contact them on VHF 13 or 16.
- **Houston Ship Channel dredging, Lighted Buoy 95 to Light 109A (Dredge Nimitz, 2026-10-14 to 2026-12-31):**
  - It starts in about a week, near the end of your route.
  - Coordinate with the dredge at least 45 minutes ahead so it can move equipment out of the channel.
  - Contact them on VHF 13, 16 or 79.
- **Cedar Bayou Channel dredging and berm construction (until 2026-12-31):**
  - It is about 0.8 nm off the route.
  - It runs 24/7.

**Aids to navigation (temporary changes, no end dates)**
- Galveston Bay Entrance Channel Lighted Buoy 12 has a temporary change (about 0.8 nm off the route).
- The Lower Galveston Bay Inner Range front and rear lights have temporary changes.
- Houston Ship Channel Light 91 is discontinued for dredging.

**Advisories**
- **Houston VTS directive:** no barge work in the Houston Ship Channel between Morgans Point and Exxon to go into or out of the USI Canal.
- **Menhaden season:** schools of fish can clog sea strainers and cooling systems (Sector Houston-Galveston bulletin).
- **Hurricane season:** a general Coast Guard bulletin applies through Nov 30. It describes Port Conditions Whiskey, X-Ray, Yankee and Zulu, where Zulu means the port is closed.

The route is only the straight line between your two points. The tool doesn't plan a navigable path, and the line probably crosses land in places. Confirm with current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, VHF broadcasts and VTS Houston-Galveston before you go. This is not navigational advice.

U.S. Coast Guard Heartland District Hurricane Season 2026 --- The 2026 Hurricane Season extends from June 1, 2026 through November 30, 2026.  Tropical storms and hurricanes often develop with little warning.  Extensive damage to small craft often results in loss of life.  All mariners, particularly operators of small fishing vessels, are reminded that advanced planning, which may prevent loss of vessel and crew, should include:  
a) Instruction of crew and passengers in location of emergency equipment and emergency procedures.
b) Pre-sailing check of vessel, machinery, and equipment for seaworthiness.
c) Installation of strong ground tackle.
d) Review of storm center evacuation procedures.
e) Knowledge of the nearest hurricane shelter or port of refuge.
f) Constant radio watch on VHF-FM Channel 16 and frequent monitoring of VHF-FM Weather Channel for National Weather Service Broadcasts.


• AIDS TO NAVIGATION/WRECKS/OBSTRUCTIONS: As a result of tropical storms and hurricanes, aids to navigation along the Gulf Coast and on structures in the Gulf of America and surrounding waters may become damaged or destroyed.  Buoys may move from assigned positions, be damaged, extinguished, sunk, or otherwise made inoperative.  Mariners should not solely rely upon the position or operation of an aid to navigation, but should employ such other available methods of determining positions.  Wrecks, submerged obstructions, and pipelines may move from charted locations or become uncovered due to the force of storm surges.  Storm surges and winds may also create shoals.  The U.S. Aids to Navigation System marking wrecks and obstructions is intended for use with nautical charts.  The exact meaning of a particular aid to navigation may not be clear to the mariner without referencing a nautical chart.  Mariners should exercise caution and report aid to navigation discrepancies and hazards to navigation to the nearest U.S. Coast Guard unit.

• LOCKS/BRIDGES/NAVIGATION STRUCTURES: Drawbridges, locks, and navigation structures along the coast may deviate from normal operating procedures in preparation for heavy weather events.  Some structures may be unable to open because of high winds, high water levels, or to facilitate evacuation of land traffic.  Mariners will be given as much notice as possible when structures are to be closed; however, these structures may close on short notice and well in advance of the storm.  Mariners should anticipate these closures and are urged to seek safe harbor as soon as possible.

• PORTS/WATERWAYS: As tropical weather approaches the Gulf Coast, all potentially affected U.S. Coast Guard Captains of the Port (COTP) will issue a series of Port Conditions to promote the safety of life, the environment, and the viability of the Marine Transportation System.  Port Conditions are issued on a set timeline prior to the arrival of gale force winds associated with a tropical activity and identify the status of the port.  Timelines associated with each port condition are subject to local modifications based upon circumstances, but are most typically issued as follows:

- WHISKEY: 72 hours in advance, OPEN to all commercial traffic. 
- X-RAY: 48 hours in advance, OPEN to all commercial traffic.
- YANKEE: 24 hours in advance, RESTRICTED with vessel traffic control measures in effect.
- ZULU: 12 hours in advance, CLOSED to all vessel traffic, except for movements or activities specifically authorized by the COTP.

• Additional requirements or actions to address port-specific safety concerns will be issued by the COTP in conjunction with each Port Condition.  After the passing of a hurricane, local COTPs will issue updates regarding the port status via Broadcast Notice to Mariners and MSIBs.  Mariners are urged to monitor all U.S. Coast Guard and National Weather Service notices and radio traffic closely throughout the Hurricane Season. This is typically a seasonal event primarily occurring in the months of March thru October (although vessels have reported Menhaden impacts year-round).  Menhaden are typically found in coastal and inland tidal waters, and can form large surface schools, appearing in near-shore Gulf waters.  Schools of fish can be drawn into the vessel’s sea chest, clogging the sea strainers, reducing cooling, and causing high water/oil temperatures. Two official Coast Guard notices intersect your track. Neither should restrict your transit tomorrow, but the check was incomplete (see below).

I checked the track as a straight line from 37.00, -76.10 to 36.88, -76.33, about 13.2 nm, with a 1 nm corridor on each side. The source was the USCG NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information layers.

**1. Marine construction: dredging, Elizabeth River (MSI #53466, CG District 5)**
- **Location:** Lambert's Point Pier 6, Norfolk. The notice polygon sits right at your end point, around 36.88, -76.33.
- **Valid:** Oct 9, 2026 to Jan 4, 2027, so it takes effect tomorrow.
- **Timing:** The notice text says dredging starts "on or about October 21, 2026". Tomorrow you probably won't meet active dredging.
- **What it describes:** The dredge KOKO V works with towing tugs and scows. Loaded scows are towed from Pier 6 to an unloader barge at Shirley's Plantation (Weanack Island).
- **Radio:** Vessels monitor VHF channel 13.
- **For you:** Expect tug and scow traffic near the Elizabeth River end of your track.

**2. Marine event: Marine Event Permit process notice (CG District 5)**
- **Valid:** Jun 3 to Nov 30, 2026.
- **What it is:** It's an administrative announcement about a new online permit application process for regattas, fireworks and similar events. Its polygon covers a very large part of the region.
- **For you:** It isn't a restriction or hazard, and you can ignore it for transit.

**Matches by category:** No hazards to navigation, safety zones, naval activity, space operations, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories or MSIBs matched in the layers that were checked.

**Limits of this check**
- **Incomplete safety-zone layer:** NAVCEN lists the `safeZoneLine_1` file but doesn't publish it (HTTP 404). Safety zones drawn as lines weren't checked. Zero safety-zone matches therefore doesn't prove there are none. This is a real gap in an area with heavy naval and commercial traffic.
- **Not covered:** Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, Light List and aids-to-navigation discrepancies, and notices without geometry. It also doesn't cover non-USCG sources such as NOAA, NGA NAVAREA warnings, weather and tides.
- **Timing:** I ran the check at the current time, not at a specific time tomorrow. Both notices would be in effect tomorrow either way. Notices issued between now and your departure won't be included.

Before you leave, check the current Broadcast Notices to Mariners and the Local Notice to Mariners for Sector Virginia. Also call the Coast Guard or listen to VHF for any safety zones in the Hampton Roads and Norfolk area. This is official-notice information, not navigational advice.

# README summary
## USCG Navigation Restriction Resolver

Checks a location, vessel route, or geographic bounding box against official U.S. Coast Guard Navigation Center (NAVCEN) Maritime Safety Information (MSI) GeoJSON layers and returns a single structured record of intersecting maritime notices. Outputs include intersecting safety zones, hazards to navigation, marine construction, marine events, naval activity, space-operation areas, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories and geospatial MSIBs, with each notice’s official text, validity windows, geometry and source provenance. Spatial processing uses a local azimuthal-equidistant projection centered on the query so nautical-mile buffers and corridors represent true distances; reported distances are geodesic on the WGS84 ellipsoid. Notices are time-classified at the query time (active, upcoming, or unknown validity) and expired records are accounted for separately. Results include per-dataset coverage metadata and status for each NAVCEN file checked, flags for unpublished or unavailable files, and a coverage note when dataset files were listed but not served. Route queries are ordered by position along the route; point and area queries are ordered by distance. Source is the NAVCEN GeoJSON layers (no third‑party data).

## Use cases

- Pre-voyage information gathering and route screening  
- Maritime operations workflows and harbor/port reconnaissance  
- Marine construction planning and project impact assessment  
- Space-operation awareness near coastlines and maritime areas  
- Autonomous agent research and automated maritime compliance checks

finalAnswer:
**12 active USCG notices fall within 2 nm of your route** (42.50,‑70.80 → 42.54,‑70.87; about 3.9 nm long). The check ran on 2026‑10‑08 against USCG NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information. The results are not complete, because one layer couldn't be checked (see the last section).

## Marine construction (3)
All three are for removal of daybeacons by AGM Marine Contractors, using dredge PRONCKAI, deck barge THING and tug SITKA. Work is 6am–8pm daily, about Sep 28 to Nov 15/16, 2026. The vessels monitor VHF‑FM 13 and 16 and work on channel 68.
- **Bowditch Ledge Daybeacon** (Salem Sound), at 42°32.4'N 070°48.7'W. It is 1.59 nm from the route.
- **Abbott Rock Daybeacon** (Salem Harbor), at 42°31.8'N 070°51.7'W. It is 0.23 nm from the route.
- **Lobster Rock Daybeacon** (Salem Harbor), at 42°32.3'N 070°52.9'W. It is 0.53 nm from the route.

## Hazard to navigation (1)
- **Bass River shoaling.** Severe shoaling has been reported between Bass River Channel Buoys 2 and 9, with a severe decrease in channel width. The notice runs to 2039. It is 0.89 nm from the route (Chart 13275).

## Marine events (8)
Regattas in Marblehead Harbor and Salem Sound, all on Chart 13275, except the Beverly reenactment on Chart 13276. Most polygons intersect the route directly.
- **Etchells New England Championships:** Oct 8–11, 11am–4pm, about 30 boats, in Salem Sound and Marblehead Harbor.
- **Nessa Keelboat High School Championships:** Oct 10, 9am–4pm, and Oct 11, 9am–12pm.
- **Beverly 400 Battle of the Hannah and Nautilus reenactment:** Oct 10, 9–11am, in Beverly Harbor off Independence Park, with 2 sailing vessels. It intersects the route's end.
- **Pumpkin Pursuit Race 2:** Oct 17 (the notice says Sunday), 12–4pm, about 15 boats.
- **Halloween Team Race:** Oct 24–25, 9am–4pm.
- **Pumpkin Pursuit Race 3:** Oct 24, 12–4pm.
- **Fall Laser ILCA Series:** Sundays, Sep 13 – Nov 22, 1–3pm, about 15 boats at 14'. The polygon intersects the route.
- **BYC MIT Tech Dinghy Frostbiting Series:** Sundays, Nov 8, 2026 – Apr 4, 2027, 12–2pm, in Marblehead Harbor. It is 0.35 nm from the route. The notice's record window starts Oct 8, but the text gives Nov 8 as the first race.

## What wasn't checked
- **Safety zones:** the USCG file for this layer (`safeZoneLine_1`) returned a 404, so safety zones were not checked. Zero safety‑zone results here does not mean none exist.
- **Other gaps:** Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, aids‑to‑navigation discrepancies, and non‑USCG sources (NOAA, NGA NAVAREA warnings) were not covered.
- **Not for navigation:** this is information only. Check current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners and VHF broadcasts before transiting.

The zone is enforced from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily, and only while construction work is under way. You may not enter, remain in or transit through it during enforcement unless the Captain of the Port New York authorizes it. Some full-channel closures are scheduled, including 22–26 June 2026, but the text says these dates may change.
- **Larchmont fireworks zone:** The database still marks it "active" because its record window runs to December 2026. The notice text says it was only enforced on July 3, 2026, from 9:00 to 10:30 p.m., and that date has passed.

This rule is effective without notice from December 3, 2024, through 5 p.m. on May 27, 2027. This area is intended for the vessels and machinery being used by personnel for the Glen Island Bridge rehabilitation project. finalAnswer:
No active USCG safety zone covers 41.35, -72.10 itself. One active zone is nearby, and the check was incomplete (details below).

**New London Harbor – Shaw Cove Entrance** (NAVCEN record MSI UID 53516)
- **Distance:** Its center is at about 41°21′01″N, 72°05′42″W (41.3503, -72.0950). That is roughly 0.23 nm from your point, so your point is inside the 5 nm search area but not inside the zone.
- **Type:** Temporary safety zone, Coast Guard District 1.
- **Area:** All navigable waters of the Thames River within a 600-foot radius of that position, near New London Waterfront Park, New London, CT.
- **Event:** A drone show. The zone was in force on September 12, 2026, from 8:15 to 9:30 p.m. The notice itself is listed as valid from 2026-09-11 to 2027-03-13.
- **Rule:** No vessel or person may enter without permission from the Captain of the Port (COTP) or a designated representative.
- **Contact:** The person in charge of the drone show is Jeff Ward, (516) 369-2107.

The 600-foot radius is about 0.1 nm, which is smaller than the 0.23 nm gap. So even while the zone is in force, it should not reach your exact coordinate. That is my own estimate. It is not a value the actor reported.

**The check was incomplete.** NAVCEN lists a dataset of line-type safety zones (`safeZoneLine_1`) but returns a 404 for it, so those records weren't checked. Zero matches for line-type zones therefore doesn't mean none exist. I also only searched safety zones, not other notice types such as hazards or marine events. The search doesn't cover Broadcast Notices to Mariners.

This is not navigational advice. Before transiting, check the current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, VHF broadcasts, and the Sector Long Island Sound COTP.

  - Work is at about 36°58'16"N 76°24'57"W, weekdays 0700–1530.
  - Vessels should keep to no wake within 500 ft and monitor VHF 13 and 16.
- MSI 53462, Kinder Morgan Bulk Terminals dredging, Newport News: 4.8 nm away, active 24 Sep 2026 to 4 Jan 2027.

I found 4 current USCG Local Notice to Mariners records within 3 nm of 21.46, -157.76 (Kaneohe Bay and Mokapu Peninsula, Oahu). All four are active as of 2026-10-08. The search is not complete, because one layer couldn't be checked (details below).

| # | MSI UID | Category | Location | Distance | Effective window |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3943 | Naval activity (gunnery exercises) | Kaneohe Bay, Sampan Channel | 0 nm (point is inside the polygon) | 2024-10-30 to 2028-06-28 |
| 2 | 23349 | Hazard to navigation | Mokapu Peninsula | 0.54 nm | 2025-07-10 to 2027-01-01 |
| 3 | 3937 | Naval activity (military operations) | Kaneohe Bay | 1.46 nm | 2024-10-30 to 2028-07-31 |
| 4 | 3944 | Naval activity (gunnery exercises) | Sector Honolulu Territorial Sea / EEZ | 1.61 nm | 2024-10-30 to 2028-07-31 |

**Details**
1. **3943, Pyramid Rock / Fort Hase / Kaneohe Bay Danger Zone**
   - The zone is closed at all times to surface craft, swimmers and divers, except authorized personnel.
   - The only listed operation for Oct 5–16 is a Wed Oct 14 helicopter SAR exercise at the Pyramid Rock lighthouse, 0900–1400.
2. **23349, Wave Energy Converter (OE-35) failure**
   - The converter's port sea duct failed structurally, and four large pieces (up to 22 MT) fell to the seafloor.
   - Further failure is possible. Mariners are asked to stay 1000 ft from the buoy.
3. **3937, military amphibious and search-and-rescue operations**
   - These may happen at any time, day or night, about 0.5 nm south of Mokapu Peninsula.
   - Contact Waterfront Operations on VHF Ch 82A or at (808) 257-2941, especially if you use sonar, to avoid endangering divers.
4. **3944, Ulupau Crater danger zone**
   - Vessels must leave the zone at best speed by the most direct route.
   - Hazardous operations are listed for Zones 1 and 2 on most days of Oct 5–16, mainly 0000–0200 and 0600–2359. There are none on Oct 10–12, and Oct 13 is 0600–2359 only.

**Coverage gap:** The Coast Guard's `safeZoneLine_1` safety-zone file is listed in its index but returns a 404 (not published). Safety-zone records in that file were not checked, so there could be safety zones near this point that aren't shown here. No expired records were excluded.

**Scope:** The data comes from the Coast Guard's NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information layers. Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, Light List data and aids-to-navigation discrepancies aren't covered. This is informational, not navigational advice, so check current official Notices to Mariners and VHF broadcasts before relying on it.

# README summary
## USCG Navigation Restriction Resolver

Checks a location, vessel route, or geographic bounding box against official U.S. Coast Guard Navigation Center (NAVCEN) Maritime Safety Information (MSI) GeoJSON layers and returns a single structured record of intersecting maritime notices. Outputs include intersecting safety zones, hazards to navigation, marine construction, marine events, naval activity, space-operation areas, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories and geospatial MSIBs, with each notice’s official text, validity windows, geometry and source provenance. Spatial processing uses a local azimuthal-equidistant projection centered on the query so nautical-mile buffers and corridors represent true distances; reported distances are geodesic on the WGS84 ellipsoid. Notices are time-classified at the query time (active, upcoming, or unknown validity) and expired records are accounted for separately. Results include per-dataset coverage metadata and status for each NAVCEN file checked, flags for unpublished or unavailable files, and a coverage note when dataset files were listed but not served. Route queries are ordered by position along the route; point and area queries are ordered by distance. Source is the NAVCEN GeoJSON layers (no third‑party data).

## Use cases

- Pre-voyage information gathering and route screening  
- Maritime operations workflows and harbor/port reconnaissance  
- Marine construction planning and project impact assessment  
- Space-operation awareness near coastlines and maritime areas  
- Autonomous agent research and automated maritime compliance checks

Yes. The USCG Navigation Center's Maritime Safety Information shows two active space-operation hazard areas within 25 nm of 33.80°N, 119.30°W. I checked as of 2026-10-08 21:07 UTC. Neither area contains your point.

**1. NASA Crew-12 reentry and splashdown, Los Angeles site (Sector Los Angeles, Territorial Sea)**
- **Distance:** about 2.3 nm from your point. This is the closest area, and its boundary nearly touches your position.
- **Effective window:** 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-20 (UTC). The notice text gives the hazardous operations as 05 Oct 16:35 UTC to 19 Oct 19:05 UTC.
- **Type:** Hazardous Warning Area, Significant National Interest.
- **Boundary:** 33.78N 119.25W → 33.75N 119.30W → 33.60N 119.30W → 33.55N 119.233W → 33.55N 119.117W → 33.617N 119.033W → 33.75N 119.033W → 33.783N 119.083W.
- **Contact:** SpaceX, regulatory@spacex.com, or VHF-FM channel 05, 06 or 16.

**2. SpaceX Starlink g15-25 launch (Sector San Diego, EEZ)**
- **Distance:** about 24.7 nm. It only just falls inside your 25 nm radius.
- **Effective window:** 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-18 (UTC).
- **Type:** Hazardous Warning Area, Commercial.
- **Shape:** a long strip running from near Point Conception, around 34.6N 120.6W, southeast to about 28.2N 117.3W.
- **Primary window:** 10 Oct 23:00Z to 11 Oct 03:25Z (Hazard Area A) or 03:43Z (Hazard Area B). Backup days run daily at the same times through 16–17 Oct.

Mariners are advised to stay clear of both areas while operations are underway.

This covers only USCG NAVCEN Local Notice to Mariners geospatial records. It does not cover Broadcast Notices to Mariners, NGA NAVAREA warnings, or records without geometry. It's also not navigational advice, so check current Notices to Mariners and VHF broadcasts before transiting.

For each chokepoint it reports latest daily transits and tanker transits, short-term (7‑day) and medium-term (30‑day) averages with year‑over‑year comparisons, a disruption level determined by percent change versus the same window one year earlier (severity tiers), 7‑day breakdowns by ship type (tanker, container, dry bulk, general cargo, ro‑ro) and average carried capacity in tons, plus optional daily history (up to 400 days). It also emits one record per active navigational warning containing NAVAREA/subregion identifiers, message metadata, full warning text, region tags (Persian Gulf/Hormuz, Red Sea/Gulf of Aden, Black Sea/Ukraine, Eastern Mediterranean, Taiwan/South China Sea, Baltic) and risk keywords (missile, firing, drone, GNSS jamming, mine, piracy, etc.). I found two active marine construction notices in the East River between 40.70,-73.98 and 40.76,-73.95. Both come from USCG NAVCEN Local Notice to Mariners data, checked on 2026-10-08.

**1. East River Main Channel, Montgomery St to E 14th St (MSI #913)**
- **Dates:** 2022-01-03 to 2026-12-30.
- **Work:** The notice covers esplanade, bulkhead and park reconstruction. The listed contractor is IPCP.
- **Hours:** 5–7 days a week, 6:00am–6:00pm.
- **Area:** A long, narrow strip along the Manhattan shoreline, from about 40.709°N, -73.984°W up to 40.727°N, -73.971°W.
- **Equipment:** Tugboat DEBRA QUINN, an inspection boat, mooring barges, a gantry crane barge, a crawler crane barge, deck barges and hopper barges.
- **Vessel moves:** Tugboats move the vessels at any time of day or night.
- **VHF:** Monitoring channels 13 and 66.
- **Guidance:** Transit at your slowest safe speed to minimize wake, and arrange passing before you go by.

**2. East River Main Channel, Water Club and E 34th St Heliport (MSI #26111)**
- **Dates:** 2025-09-01 to 2027-07-05. The notice text says work runs from September 15, 2025.
- **Work:** Diver operations at the marginal wharf platforms. The listed contractor is Phoenix Marine Co.
- **Hours:** 6:00am–2:00pm.
- **Area:** A small polygon between about 40.7399°N and 40.7427°N, near -73.972°W.
- **Equipment:** One crane barge, one material barge and one work platform barge.
- **VHF:** Monitoring channel 9.
- **Guidance:** Use extreme caution and transit at the slowest safe speed to minimize wake.

**Coverage limits:**
- The data doesn't include Broadcast Notices to Mariners.
- It also leaves out bridge work, notices without geometry, and non-USCG sources such as NOAA and NGA.
- Before transiting, check the current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, and listen on VHF. This is not navigational advice.

finalAnswer:
Yes. A search of the Coast Guard's NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information datasets found two active marine construction notices within 5 nautical miles of 38.89, -77.05. I checked all four marine construction layers, and none had errors.

**1. Tidal Basin and West Potomac Park Seawall Rehabilitation** (MSI UID 270)
- **Distance:** About 0.16 nm from your point. The notice area is a polygon along the West Potomac Park shoreline, and the point itself falls just outside it.
- **Dates:** Active from 2024-09-09 to 2027-02-01. Waterside work is expected to finish by the end of 2026.
- **Work:** Cianbro Corporation is doing the work for the National Park Service. The notice lists:
  - Two temporary trestles, about 94 ft into the river and about 55 ft into the Tidal Basin.
  - Turbidity curtains and two monitoring buoys.
  - Crane barges, material barges and other boats.
- **Work area:** It runs along the shoreline from Arlington Memorial Bridge to the Inlet Bridge.
- **Mariner request:** Stay out of the work area and keep wake to a minimum.
- **Waterway and district:** Listed under the Chesapeake Channel / Potomac River, Coast Guard District 5.

**2. Long Bridge and Pedestrian Bridge construction moorings** (MSI UID 31521)
- **Distance:** About 0.97 nm from your point, at 38°52'55.9"N, 77°01'54.9"W in the Georgetown Channel, Coast Guard District 5.
- **Dates:** Active from 2025-11-04 to 2030-01-01.
- **Work:** North Skanska Flatiron Joint Venture is installing mooring anchors and buoys. It is driving 36" steel piles and building a trestle across the Washington Channel to widen the CSX Long Bridge. The trestle will stop about 200 ft from the existing bridge.
- **Mooring location:** The anchors will sit about 130 ft from the southeast shore, between the CSX Long Bridge and the I-395 Bridge.

**Limits**
- The search did not cover Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, records without geometry, or non-Coast Guard sources such as NOAA or NGA.
- This is not navigational advice. Before transiting, check current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, VHF broadcasts and official charts.

The data comes from the Actor `rhincodontypus/uscg-navigation-restriction-resolver`. Its source is https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/msi.

finalAnswer:
**Official USCG navigation notices within 10 nm of 39.47 N, 74.29 W**

I checked the U.S. Coast Guard's NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information layers. This point is at Little Egg Inlet, NJ. The search found 17 notices: 12 active and 5 with no stated validity window.

**Hazards to navigation (shoaling), all active**
- **MSI 58, Little Egg Inlet, 0.3 nm away:** Shoaling lies between Buoys 1 and 4 and extends toward the channel. Low-tide depths were observed at about 4 ft, and the inlet can shift at any time. The notice runs through 2029-07-05.
- **MSI 2519, 2.2 nm away, near the NJ ICW Junction Lighted Buoy "LEI":** Shoaling is developing. The notice runs through 2027-04-24.
- **MSI 12588, 3.1 nm away, near NJ ICW Daybeacon 129 and Buoy 130A:** Shoaling based on an Army Corps of Engineers survey. It runs through 2029-06-27.
- **MSI 12587, 4.3 nm away, near NJ ICW Light 141 and Daybeacon 144:** Shoaling based on an Army Corps survey. It runs through 2029-06-27.
- **MSI 2572, 4.8 nm away, between NJ ICW Daybeacon 159 and Buoy 163:** The area is reported **impassable at low tide**. It runs through 2029-07-05.
- **MSI 24653, 9.9 nm away, near NJ ICW Daybeacons 207 and 209:** Shoaling based on a 2023 survey. The text says "To: 2025-08-01", but the record is still flagged active through 2029-06-27. Treat that one with caution.

**Marine construction (dredging), all active**
- **MSI 54372, 3.9 nm away, NJ ICW near Great Bay:** The Dredge Fullerton works 24 hours a day, Monday to Saturday, from 2026-09-28 to 2026-12-30. It monitors VHF 13 and 16, and mariners should transit with caution.
- **MSI 46675, 5.4 nm away, Little Egg Harbor:** Dredges work 24/7 from 2026-06-12 to 2027-01-31. Submerged pipeline crossings are marked with buoys and yellow flashing lights. It monitors VHF 16 and 65, and vessels should go slowly.
- **MSI 45757 and 45758, about 7.8 nm away, Absecon Inlet:** Staging areas for a beach renourishment project, active through 2026-10-19. They monitor VHF 13 and 16.
- **MSI 52564, 8.4 nm away, Clam Creek:** Cutter-suction dredge SCROD, 24/7 through 2027-01-08. The channel stays open but narrower, with submerged pipeline crossings marked by buoys. It monitors VHF 16 and 65.

**Temporary aids to navigation (validity not stated)**
- Temporary Danger Buoys on the NJ ICW: 147 (4.2 nm), 152 (4.8 nm), 167 (5.7 nm), 170A (6.4 nm) and 171 (6.2 nm).

**Marine event**
- **MSI 45232:** A general notice about the marine event permit process. It covers a large area, and nothing in it is a hazard.

**Limits of this check**
- **Safety zones weren't checked.** NAVCEN's safety-zone file (`safeZoneLine_1`) was unavailable, so a lack of safety-zone results doesn't mean none exist.
- **Other sources weren't covered.** The check leaves out Broadcast Notices to Mariners, NOAA chart data, NGA NAVAREA warnings, bridge notices and aids-to-navigation discrepancies.
- **Not for navigation.** This is information only. Check current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, VHF broadcasts and official charts before you transit.

Yes. The USCG's Maritime Safety Information shows two active hazard-to-navigation notices within 5 nm of 38.68 N, 75.10 W. Both are shoaling reports in Rehoboth Bay, Delaware, in Coast Guard District 5.

**Hazards to navigation**
1. **Shoaling at Rehoboth Bay (MSI #61)**
   - It is about 0.15 nm from your position, at 38.6825 N, 75.1001 W.
   - Shoaling runs from the entrance to the Rehoboth–Lewes canal south to Rehoboth Bay Channel Buoy 3 (LLNR 2100). Depths there are 2–4 ft at mean low water.
   - The notice is listed as valid from 2024-08-01 to 2027-11-13.
2. **Shoaling in Baker's Channel (MSI #62)**
   - It is about 2.7 nm south of your position, around 38.631–38.634 N, 75.093–75.099 W.
   - It lies between Baker's Channel Lighted Buoys 1A and 1B and between Lighted Buoys 5 and 6. DNREC has placed two "DANGER SHOAL" warning buoys.
   - The feed lists an end date of 2029-07-05. The notice text itself says "From 2024-08-01 To 2025-08-19", so the dates conflict. It may be stale, but the feed still shows it as active.

**Other active notices nearby**
- **Dredging (MSI #51875):** The Dredge Rockbridge is working in the Lewes and Rehoboth Canal from 2026-08-24 to 2027-03-11. The area is about 0.4 nm from your position. Pipelines, anchors and cables are in the water. Vessels should call the dredge on VHF 13 or 16 before passing and stay clear.
- **Marine event (MSI #45232):** This is a broad regional notice about the permit application process. It isn't a specific hazard.

**Coverage gaps**
- One safety-zone line dataset (`safeZoneLine_1`) is listed by NAVCEN but not published, so it wasn't checked. Safety-zone line features near you could be missing from the results.
- The search doesn't cover Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, aids-to-navigation discrepancies, or non-USCG sources such as NOAA or NGA.

This is for information only, not for navigation. Check current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners and official charts before you go.

I checked the USCG NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information layers within 5 nm of 29.73, -95.03. That returned 13 notices: 10 active and 3 with no stated validity dates. The safety-zone layer was not published (HTTP 404), so safety zones were not checked. A "no safety zones" result would not be reliable here. Check the USCG Sector Houston-Galveston and the Local Notice to Mariners directly for those.

**Closest to your point (within 0.5 nm)**
- **Dredging near Buoy 95 to Light 109A (0.41 nm away).** The notice is active, running 2026-10-05 to 2027-01-01, with work stated as 2026-10-14 to 12-31.
  - The Dredge NIMITZ works 24/7 with a crane barge, deck barges, a fuel barge and tenders, and pumps spoil by pipeline to Alexander Island.
  - Vessels should coordinate with the dredge at least 45 minutes ahead.
  - VHF 13, 16 and 79. Contact: (713) 913-7207.
- **VTS directive for the USI Canal / San Jacinto Bay Channel (0.08 nm away).** This is an MSIB in effect through 2035.
  - VTS Houston-Galveston directs no barge work in the Houston Ship Channel between Morgans Point and Exxon for going into or out of the USI Canal.

**Other active notices on the Houston Ship Channel (about 2.8 to 4.4 nm away)**
- **Barbours Terminal Channel / Morgans Point dredging and bulkhead construction (2.8 nm).** Active 2025-04-07 to 2027-07-01, 24/7. Dive operations may occur, so watch for dive flags. VHF 13 and 16.
- **Dredge DB CATALINA near Barbours Cut (3.2 nm).** Active from 2026-08-10, with the notice ending 10-31 or "until further notice". It requests wake and surge consideration and 30 minutes' notice. VHF 13 and 81. Contact: (562) 772-5898.
- **Dredge R.B. WEEKS between Lights 78 and 92 (3.7 nm).** The notice window ends 2026-10-11, with the text saying through 10-10. Vessels are asked to avoid meeting or overtaking near the dredges. VHF 13 and 16.
- **Cedar Bayou Channel (3.8 to 4.5 nm).**
  - Dredge GENERAL EISENHOWER is digging flotation access channels near Atkinson Island, through 2026-12-31.
  - Two temporary barge mooring areas with piles are in place through 2027-02-28.

**Temporary aid changes (no dates given)**
- Light 124A is discontinued for dredging (2.6 nm).
- Light 91 is discontinued for dredging (3.7 nm).
- San Jacinto River Buoy 13 is discontinued (4.4 nm).

**Broader advisories covering the area**
- **MSIB 26-08, Menhaden season.** Fish can clog sea strainers and cause loss of propulsion or firefighting water pressure. Active through 2026-11-01.
- **District 8 Hurricane Season 2026 MSIB.** Active through 2026-12-01. It describes Port Conditions WHISKEY, X-RAY, YANKEE and ZULU.

This covers only USCG NAVCEN geospatial records. It does not include Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, NOAA or NGA warnings, or records without geometry. It is not navigational advice. Confirm with current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, VTS Houston-Galveston, or VHF broadcasts before transiting.

U.S. Coast Guard Heartland District Hurricane Season 2026 --- The 2026 Hurricane Season extends from June 1, 2026 through November 30, 2026.  Tropical storms and hurricanes often develop with little warning.  Extensive damage to small craft often results in loss of life.  All mariners, particularly operators of small fishing vessels, are reminded that advanced planning, which may prevent loss of vessel and crew, should include:  
a) Instruction of crew and passengers in location of emergency equipment and emergency procedures.
b) Pre-sailing check of vessel, machinery, and equipment for seaworthiness.
c) Installation of strong ground tackle.
d) Review of storm center evacuation procedures.
e) Knowledge of the nearest hurricane shelter or port of refuge.
f) Constant radio watch on VHF-FM Channel 16 and frequent monitoring of VHF-FM Weather Channel for National Weather Service Broadcasts.


• AIDS TO NAVIGATION/WRECKS/OBSTRUCTIONS: As a result of tropical storms and hurricanes, aids to navigation along the Gulf Coast and on structures in the Gulf of America and surrounding waters may become damaged or destroyed.  Buoys may move from assigned positions, be damaged, extinguished, sunk, or otherwise made inoperative.  Mariners should not solely rely upon the position or operation of an aid to navigation, but should employ such other available methods of determining positions.  Wrecks, submerged obstructions, and pipelines may move from charted locations or become uncovered due to the force of storm surges.  Storm surges and winds may also create shoals.  The U.S. Aids to Navigation System marking wrecks and obstructions is intended for use with nautical charts.  The exact meaning of a particular aid to navigation may not be clear to the mariner without referencing a nautical chart.  Mariners should exercise caution and report aid to navigation discrepancies and hazards to navigation to the nearest U.S. Coast Guard unit.

• LOCKS/BRIDGES/NAVIGATION STRUCTURES: Drawbridges, locks, and navigation structures along the coast may deviate from normal operating procedures in preparation for heavy weather events.  Some structures may be unable to open because of high winds, high water levels, or to facilitate evacuation of land traffic.  Mariners will be given as much notice as possible when structures are to be closed; however, these structures may close on short notice and well in advance of the storm.  Mariners should anticipate these closures and are urged to seek safe harbor as soon as possible.

• PORTS/WATERWAYS: As tropical weather approaches the Gulf Coast, all potentially affected U.S. Coast Guard Captains of the Port (COTP) will issue a series of Port Conditions to promote the safety of life, the environment, and the viability of the Marine Transportation System.  Port Conditions are issued on a set timeline prior to the arrival of gale force winds associated with a tropical activity and identify the status of the port.  Timelines associated with each port condition are subject to local modifications based upon circumstances, but are most typically issued as follows:

- WHISKEY: 72 hours in advance, OPEN to all commercial traffic. 
- X-RAY: 48 hours in advance, OPEN to all commercial traffic.
- YANKEE: 24 hours in advance, RESTRICTED with vessel traffic control measures in effect.
- ZULU: 12 hours in advance, CLOSED to all vessel traffic, except for movements or activities specifically authorized by the COTP.

• Additional requirements or actions to address port-specific safety concerns will be issued by the COTP in conjunction with each Port Condition.  After the passing of a hurricane, local COTPs will issue updates regarding the port status via Broadcast Notice to Mariners and MSIBs.  Mariners are urged to monitor all U.S. Coast Guard and National Weather Service notices and radio traffic closely throughout the Hurricane Season. This is typically a seasonal event primarily occurring in the months of March thru October (although vessels have reported Menhaden impacts year-round).  Menhaden are typically found in coastal and inland tidal waters, and can form large surface schools, appearing in near-shore Gulf waters.  Schools of fish can be drawn into the vessel’s sea chest, clogging the sea strainers, reducing cooling, and causing high water/oil temperatures.  In extreme cases, intake of these fish have choked entire coolant systems resulting in engine auto slowdowns or automatic shutdowns.  Any system that takes suction from the sea could be at risk.  The Lone Star Harbor Safety Committee’s Causality Analysis Workgroup (CAWG) developed Recommended Best Practices and a “Vessel Questionnaire on Cooling Water Impacts by Menhaden Fish".  All deep draft vessels operators are encouraged to follow the Recommended Best Practices and are asked to complete and submit the questionnaire to info@theagcteam.com. The data comes from the USCG NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information layers, checked on 2026-10-08 at about 21:10 UTC. 52 notices are active and 1 has unknown validity.

**Gaps in coverage**
- **Safety-zone line layer:** NAVCEN lists `safeZoneLine_1` but hasn't published it, so it wasn't checked. Safety zones drawn as lines may be missing.
- **Marine construction:** 30 notices matched, but my output was cut off after 15 of them. The 15 I didn't read are not listed below.
- **Not covered at all:** Broadcast Notices to Mariners (BNM), bridge notices, Light List data, aids-to-navigation discrepancies, and NOAA, NGA and AIS sources. Check VHF broadcasts and NAVCEN directly for these.
- **Area:** Several notices fall in or beyond the Long Island Sound, East River and Hudson River edges of your box.

**Safety zones (3)**
- **Glen Island Approach Bridge, New Rochelle (Long Island Sound):** two overlapping zones, a Temporary Regulated Navigation Zone and a Captain of the Port restriction. They are enforced 7 a.m.–5 p.m. daily, only while construction is under way, through 2027-05-27. Entry needs Captain of the Port New York permission.
- **Hudson River, Manhattan (Pier 66 area, around 40°45′N):** safety zone from 2026-05-01 to 2029-01-20. Entry needs permission from the Captain of the Port, on VHF channel 16 or at 718-354-4353. Community sailing and human-powered vessels can pass through the southern part, east of Lighted Hazard Buoy D.

**Hazards to navigation (11)**
- **UConn research chambers, Long Island Sound (~40°53′N, 73°43.8′W):** two buoy-marked stations through 2026-10-30.
- **Sunken hopper barge, Anchorage 21-A, Upper Bay (~40°39.6′N, 74°01.9′W):** wreck marked by buoys with white strobes, through 2027-03-27.
- **Shoaling reported at these locations:**
  - Passaic River, at the Point-No-Point Bridge.
  - Great Kills Harbor, between buoys 6 and 8.
  - Sheepshead Bay: two notices, one reporting only 2 ft at low tide near buoys 6 and 7.
  - Raunt Channel (Jamaica Bay): less than 5 ft near buoy 6.
  - Arthur Kill, Tremley Point Reach, between lighted buoys 34 and 32.
  - Shrewsbury River, near lighted buoy 5.
  - Claremont Terminal Channel: draft restricted to 13 ft plus tide, with a maximum of 18 ft.

**Marine events (8)**
- **Swims around Manhattan:** multiple dates through 2026-10-13, with the last ones on 10/12 and 10/13. Contact the swim safety officer on VHF channel 6.
- **Upper Bay sailing regattas:** Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday evenings (6:30–8:00 p.m.) on VHF channel 68, through mid-October. Separate Wed/Thu/Sat/Sun races run through 10/18 on VHF channel 71.
- **Raritan Bay regattas:** two notices, several days a week, through late 2026 or early January 2027. Contact the race officer on VHF channel 9 or 71.
- **Fireworks near Stepping Stone Park, Kings Point:** 2026-10-11, 6:45–7:45 p.m., with a 320-ft fallout radius. The notice window runs to 10/12, so it may already be over.

**Temporary change (1)**
- **United Nations Security Zone Coast Guard mooring buoy, East River (~40°44.6′N, 73°57.9′W):** newly established. It has no dates or description, so its validity is unknown.

**Marine construction (15 of 30 read)**
- **Hudson River:**
  - Pier 94 pile repair, through 2027-06-25, on VHF channel 13 with 24-hour notice for vessel moves.
  - Liberty State Park barges, through 2026-10-31.
  - Manhattan Cruise Terminal dredging, 24 hours a day through 2026-10-10, on channels 13, 16 and 78.
  - North Cove Marina dredging, 2026-10-01 to 2027-10-02, on channels 13, 16 and 65–75.
- **East River and Harlem River:**
  - Pier 36 pile repair, through 2028-11-04.
  - Grace Industries crane operations (~40°42.3′N, 73°58.96′W), through 2026-12-31. Use slow speed and call channel 16, 13 or 61A.
  - Brooklyn Bridge Park Pier 4 removal, to 2026-12-01.
  - Governors Island pedestrian bridge and fender wharf rehabilitation, from 2026-08-24, through 2026-11-30 on the notice.
  - Newtown Creek seawall work and Harlem River demolition (125th–132nd St.), through 2027-08-31.
  - Hunts Point fender replacement, through 2027-06-30.
- **Elsewhere:**
  - Port Liberty / Port Jersey terminal pile work, through 2027-03-01.
  - Kill Van Kull core borings near the Bayonne Bridge, through 2026-10-31.
  - Port Newark maintenance dredging, through 2026-10-31.
  - Gowanus Canal remediation dredging, through 2026-11-16, on channels 13 and 16.

From: 2024-12-16 To: 2027-05-31

The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for certain waters of Long Island Sound in the vicinity of the Glen Island Approach Bridge, New Rochelle, NY, for construction vessels and machinery involved in the rehabilitation project of the bridge. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with the bridge construction between December 2, 2024, through May 27, 2027. When enforced, this regulation prohibits persons and vessels from being in the safety zone unless authorized by the Captain of the Port New York or a designated representative.

DATES:
This rule is effective without notice from December 3, 2024, through 5 p.m. on May 27, 2027. For the purposes of enforcement, actual notice will be used from midnight on December 2, 2024, until December 3, 2024. This rule will only be enforced during periods when construction operations at the bridge are in progress.
Comments and related material must be received by the Coast Guard on or before March 3, 2025.

ADDRESSES:
To view documents mentioned in this preamble as being available in the docket, go to https://www.regulations.gov, type USCG-2024-0956 in the search box and click “Search.” Next, in the Document Type column, select “Supporting &amp; Related Material.”

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
If you have questions about this rule, call or email Jeffrey Yunker, Waterways Management Division, U.S. Coast Guard Sector New York; telephone 718-354-4195, email Jeffrey.M.Yunker@uscg.mil.

IV. Discussion of the Rule
This rule establishes a safety zone from 7 a.m. until 5 p.m. each day starting on midnight December 2, 2024, through May 27, 2027. The safety zone will only be enforced during periods when construction operations at the Glen Island Bridge rehabilitation project are in progress. The anticipated dates for the windows of full channel closures are from 7 a.m. on December 2, 2024, through 5 p.m. on December 20, 2024; from 7 a.m. on February 3, 2025, through 5 p.m. on May 22, 2025; and from 7 a.m. on October 2, 2025, through 5 p.m. on April 29, 2026. The Coast Guard will make notice of the safety zone via the Local Notice to Mariners and issue a Broadcast Notice to Mariners via marine channel 16 (VHF-FM) as soon as practicable in advance of these scheduled closures. All these dates are tentative and subject to change due to weather, supply chain delays, or other unforeseen circumstances. This rule remains effective through May 27, 2027, in case the project is delayed due to unforeseen circumstances. The area regulated by the safety zone will encompass the waters around the Glen Island Bridge and will cover all navigable waters, from surface to bottom, within the area formed by connecting the following latitude and longitude points in the following order:

40°53′18.58″ N 73°46′56.26″ W; thence to 40°53′22.08″ N 73°46′59.39″ W; thence north along the shore to 40°53′23.8″ N 73°46′57.51″ W; thence to 40°53′19.15″ N 73°46′52.54″ W and thence south along the shore back to the point of origin. This area is intended for the vessels and machinery being used by personnel for the Glen Island Bridge rehabilitation project. The duration of the zone is intended to ensure the safety of personnel, vessels, and these navigable waters during the bridge construction. No vessel or person will be permitted to enter the safety zone without obtaining permission from the COTP or a designated representative.

The Coast Guard will make notice of the safety zone via the Local Notice to Mariners and issue a Broadcast Notice to Mariners via marine channel 16 (VHF-FM) as soon as practicable in response to an emergency or hazardous condition.

§ 165.T01-0336 Safety Zone; Hudson River, Manhattan, NY

(a) Location. The following area is a safety zone: All waters of the Hudson River from surface to bottom, encompassed by a line connecting the following points beginning at 40°45′20.32″ N, 074°00′23.84″ W; thence to 40°45′23.34″ N, 074°00′30.60″ W; thence to 40°45′24.03″ N, 074°00′40.85″ W; thence to 40°45′18.89″ N, 074°00′48.18″ W; thence to 40°45′13.80″ N, 074°00′48.64" W; thence to 40°45′08.03″ N, 074°00′46.44″ W; thence to 40°45′07.51″ N, 074°00′37.61″W; thence to 40°45′09.18″ N, 074°00′36.37″ W; thence to 40°45′06.70″ N, 074°00′30.78″W; thence returning along the Manhattan shoreline to the beginning point.  These coordinates are based on the World Geodetic System (WGS 84) / North American Datum 83 (NAD 83). 

(b)  Definitions.  As used in this section, designated representative means a Coast Guard Patrol Commander, including a Coast Guard coxswain, petty officer, or other officer operating a Coast Guard vessel and a Federal, State, and local officer with law enforcement authority designated by or assisting the Captain of the Port New York (COTP) in the enforcement of the safety zone.
(c)  Regulations.  (1) Under the general safety zone regulations in subpart C of this part, you may not enter the safety zone described in paragraph (a) of this section unless authorized by the COTP or the COTP's designated representative. 

(2)  To seek permission to enter, contact the COTP or the COTP’s representative on VHF-FM channel 16 or by telephone at (718) 354-4353.  Those in the safety zone must comply with all lawful orders or directions given to them by the COTP or the COTP’s designated representative. 

(3)  Hudson River Community Sailing Vessels and Human Powered Vessels transiting directly to or from the Pier 66 area may transit through the southern area of the safety zone to the east of the Hudson River Cofferdam Lighted Hazard Buoy D (LLNR 37663.3) unless otherwise directed by the COTP or the COTPs designated representative. 

(d)  Enforcement period.  This section will be subject to enforcement from 12:01 a.m. on May 1, 2026, to 11:59 p.m. on January 20, 2029. If the project is completed before January 20, 2029, enforcement of the safety zone will be suspended, and notice given via Local Notice to Mariners.  The Coast Guard Northeast District Local Notice to Mariners can be found at: https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/maritime-safety-information.

The University of Connecticut Marine Sciences will conduct scientific research in New York Long Island Sound from July 2 to October 30, 2026. The project involves the deployment of four autonomous respiration chambers at four specific stations: Station 1 at 40°53'02.219" N, 73°43'50.339" W; Station 2 at 40°53'04.020" N, 73°43'45.959" W; Station 3 at 40°57'23.999" N, 73°34'59.400" W; and Station 4 at 40°57'24.420" N, 73°34'57.960" W. finalAnswer:
I checked your route (48.40, -123.40 to 48.30, -124.60, about 48 nm) against USCG NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information, using a 5 nm corridor on each side. I found one active notice.

**Active notice: TESS Advisory, Marine Wildlife Migration (Strait of Juan de Fuca)**
- **Issued by:** Sector Puget Sound, Coast Guard District 13. The record is MSI #43913.
- **Effective:** 18 May to 1 Nov 2026. The text itself says the ECHO Program measure runs 1 Jun to 31 Oct 2026.
- **Where it applies:** A polygon that your track crosses, roughly 40% of the way along the route. It covers the Canadian inshore side of the Strait, between about 48.27–48.54°N and 123.82–124.52°W.
- **What it says:** The ECHO Program voluntary inshore route alteration is active for all tugs. It aims to reduce underwater noise for at-risk whales.
  - If it is safe and operationally feasible, tugs are asked to use either the outbound shipping lane or the inshore route alteration zone.
  - They should keep a 1,000 m buffer from the traffic separation scheme (TSS).
  - The zone is 1,500 m wide and about 28 nm long. It runs from 48°18'37"N, 123°52'21"W to 48°28'53"N, 124°31'33"W.
  - More information: https://www.portvancouver.com/echo
- **Who it affects:** The measure is voluntary and aimed at tugs. If you aren't a tug it's mostly informational, but be aware of the traffic and whale-protection activity in that area.

**Nothing found in these categories:** hazards to navigation, marine construction, marine events, naval activity, space operations, temporary changes, and Marine Safety Information Bulletins (MSIBs).

**Gaps in the check**
- **Safety zones, partly unchecked:** One official safety-zone file (`safeZoneLine_1`) is listed by NAVCEN but wasn't published (HTTP 404), so line-type safety zones weren't checked. Check the NAVCEN MSI page (https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/msi) for safety zones directly.
- **Sources not covered:** The check doesn't include Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, aids-to-navigation discrepancies, or records without geometry. It also doesn't include non-USCG sources such as NOAA, NGA NAVAREA warnings, or Canadian Coast Guard notices.
- **Canadian waters:** Much of your route is near or in Canadian waters, so also check the Canadian Coast Guard NOTSHIP and NAVWARN notices.

Before you go, check the current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners and the VHF broadcasts. This is not navigational advice.
